acceptance: The owner's decision on where the check runs and how it writes issues is recorded in context before implementation starts.

A scheduled job applies the carried patches in manifest order to upstream main and to the latest final tag, and reports per patch: applies, conflicts (with files and git's error), or applies with no change (reported as a retirement candidate, not a failure).

A drift finding opens or updates one fork issue keyed by patch id and upstream commit, using the controller's marker and App-authored issue conventions; it is closed when the patch applies again or is retired.
tests/test_downstream_contract.py still passes, including the rule that write capability is confined to the controller publisher (or an owner-approved, tested change to that rule).
Tests cover a patch that stops applying because upstream changed its context, and a patch that upstream already contains.
context:
Purpose: lowers the risk that the next upstream release stops on a conflict, which would fail the core item sqlglot-e2e-first-release-certification (BenchBox-dev/BenchBox tracker; cross-tracker needs are not possible).

Decision gate (owner, before implementation): (a) run the check inside benchbox-upstream.yml's prepare job and let the existing publish job write issues (no contract change), or (b) a separate workflow, which needs an owner-approved change to test_write_capability_is_confined_to_the_controller_publisher. Also decide cadence (daily recommended) and whether drift against upstream main or only against tags raises an issue (main is earlier warning but noisier). Record the choice here.

Verification rubric: (1) new tests fail before and pass after; (2) full downstream test suite and contract tests pass; (3) a dry-run dispatch on the fork shows the per-patch report in the job summary against current upstream main; (4) a reproduction against the v30.30.0 manifest and upstream v30.31.0 reports sqlite-date-extraction and sqlite-date-day-arithmetic as conflicting.

Guardrails: the check only runs git apply on upstream content and never executes upstream code; no push, branch, pull request or label write; GITHUB_TOKEN stays read-only and the App token is the only write capability; one issue per patch and upstream commit (no issue per run); respects BENCHBOX_UPSTREAM_ENABLED and dry_run like the controller; changes to .github/workflows go through a human-reviewed fork PR.

Owner decision 2026-11-14 (choice dialog): run the drift check inside the controller's prepare job and let the existing App-token publish job write issues (no change to the write-confinement contract test); daily with the controller; probe upstream main only (the tag path is the refresh itself); one issue per drifting patch, body updated as upstream main moves, closed when the patch applies again; the run that first raises or changes a drift issue fails, later unchanged runs stay green.

Delivered in https://github.com/BenchBox-dev/benchbox-sqlglot/pull/90, merged as 19ddf096438b3a9d1ef815bdb6e59473d463939f (20/20 checks passed). 132 downstream tests pass (controller, refresh, contract, delivery, distribution). Rubric: (1) new controller tests (drift lifecycle, already-contained, probe failure, event pass, prepare exit) fail without the change (new symbols) and pass; (2) contract tests pass unchanged, write capability still confined to publish; (3) Live dry-run dispatch on main (run 43604630101): outcome up-to-date; drift probe reported conflict on spark-databricks-regexp-trunc (tests/dialects/test_exasol.py, tests/dialects/test_oracle.py) against upstream main; planned upsert_drift_issue; prepare failed with 'Needs follow-up: Carried patch spark-databricks-regexp-trunc no longer applies to upstream main (conflict)'; readiness succeeded; publish skipped (dry run). The next scheduled run opens that drift issue. (4) replay of the v30.30.0 manifest (860a2bce7) against upstream v30.31.0 reports conflict on sqlite-date-extraction (sqlglot/generators/sqlite.py), the issue #88 failure; only the first failing patch is reported because patches apply in order.
description: The controller applies the carried patches to upstream only when it refreshes onto a new tag. Upstream v30.31.0 added SQLiteGenerator.datesub_sql (tobymao/sqlglot#8931, merged 2026-11-10) at the spot where carried patches sqlite-date-day-arithmetic and sqlite-date-extraction insert, so the scheduled refresh stopped with outcome conflict (issue #88) on release day and needed a hand refresh (#89). The overlap was visible on upstream main before the tag, but nothing checks carried patches against unreleased upstream commits. With 24 carried patches, many on sqlglot/generators/sqlite.py, an active upstream file, each release risks the same stop.
